title: Why start here?
text:
Most people arrive with one of three things in mind, and the planner can work from whichever you know.

- **A gig, performer or theme** – you know who or what you want to see, even if it is only the support act you half-remember. Type it in the search box and the planner finds the dates.
- **A place** – you are going somewhere and want to know what is on nearby.
- **Some dates** – you are free on certain days and want to see what is on.

The three buttons only open the right controls first. You can combine them, for example search for a performer *and* narrow it to one part of the country.

title: Why say where?
text:
A gig is only useful if you can get to it, so this keeps the list to a sensible distance.

- Type a **town or postcode**, or a **venue** if you know it.
- Set how many **miles** you are happy to travel from there. If you are visiting an area rather than travelling from home, use the place you will be staying.

Distances are straight-line estimates scaled up for roads, not a routed journey.

title: Why choose dates?
text:
Gigs happen on particular nights, so the dates you choose decide what you see.

- Use the **quick buttons** for this weekend or the next week or month.
- Or set exact **From** and **To** dates, up to a year ahead.

If you are looking for one particular act, choose a longer range (the **Next 12 months** button is handy): their next date may be months away.

title: Why filter by type?
text:
The listings mix storytelling, music, poetry and folk nights, and not everyone wants all of them.

- Untick the types you are not interested in.
- **One-off and touring shows only** hides regular club nights, which can otherwise crowd out special events when you are searching for a theme.
- The checkbox under the map shows or hides the other venues in reach as grey pins.

title: Why pick a gig?
text:
A few days of gigs works best when it is built around one you really want to see: the **anchor**. Everything else is arranged around it.

- Use the **date strip** to jump to one day. Darker days have more on.
- Choose **Plan around this gig** on the one you want. The list then folds away (use *Change gig* to bring it back) and you move on to filling in the nights around it.

title: What is the trip?
text:
This is your plan so far: one gig a night, in date order.

- You can **copy** the plan, add it to your **calendar**, or download it to share.
- **Copy link** gives you a link that reopens this plan, so you can send it to a friend. It does not include the place you entered.
- The travel figures are straight-line estimates scaled up for roads, so treat them as a guide.

Every stop is a suggestion. Check the event's own page for times and booking before you travel.

title: Why add nights around it?
text:
A trip is more worthwhile when each night has something on. These columns show the nights before and after your gig, with gigs within reach of the *previous stop*.

- Set **how many nights** either side and **how far** you will go between stops.
- Click performers to narrow down who you would like to see.
- **Add to plan** puts one event on a night. The next night's distances are then measured from it, so the trip stays practical.
